thread:
anya: quick sync — i'm wrapping up the SDK surface doc for pagination + transport choices. want a short sanity-check on the approach i'm proposing before i convert it to an RFC. TL;DR: keep page-based sync iterators, provide async iterators for async runtimes, expose an explicit opaque 'bookmark' string on pages (instead of implicit cursor objects), and treat page fetches as idempotent for retry semantics. transports: default http/1.1 chunked + http/2 support; websocket only as opt-in for low-latency pushing. thoughts?

matt: +1 on the explicit bookmark. makes cross-lang parity easier. small nit — call it `bookmark` not `resume_token` to avoid implying internal format.

sophia: question on the "page fetches are idempotent" bit — if the server does side-effects during page generation (rare, but possible for some endpoints), we need a way to opt out of automatic retries. so: default retry for list endpoints, but allow `retry: "none"` per-call.

juan: i sketched a couple ergonomic examples. python sync:
```py
for page in client.list_documents(page_size=200):
    for doc in page.items:
        process(doc)
    # bookmark is opaque string you can store
    bookmark = page.bookmark
```
python async:
```py
async for page in client.list_documents_async(page_size=200):
    ...
```
TS/JS async iterator (node & browser):
```ts
for await (const page of client.listDocuments({pageSize: 200})) {
  page.items.forEach(process)
  const bm = page.bookmark
}
```
Go sync-ish: iterator pattern: `it.Next() bool`, `it.Page() []Document`, `it.Bookmark() string`, `it.Err()` — keeps it idiomatic.

lisa: two operational tradeoffs to call out:
- chunked HTTP/2 streaming can reduce tail latency vs polling pages, but it's harder to route through some CDNs / enterprise proxies.
- websockets allow server-driven deltas (useful for near-real-time usecases) but add complexity around auth refresh and reconnect semantics.
recommend defaulting to plain HTTP pages + optional streamed endpoints that return the same page shape incrementally (so client code can treat them uniformly).

anya: good points. on retries, proposal: default backoff: exponential with full jitter, 100ms base, max 5s, attempts capped at 5. only retry on idempotent error classes (5xx, 429, network). allow caller override `retry_policy` per-call. also include `client.retry.disable()` for debug.

matt: about the bookmark format — server should promise opacity + monotonicity: clients must treat it as blob; server may encode region/model/version in it in future for routing. make sure we version the bookmark (prefix like `v1:`) so older clients are safe.

sophia: ergonomics for partial consumption: if a user stops iterating mid-page, do we guarantee the bookmark points at the start of next page or at first unconsumed item? simpler: bookmark always represents the start of the next page (server-side page boundary). document that consumers wanting item-level resume should use streaming with per-item offsets.

juan: followup on pagination size: server will recommend defaults but client SDKs should expose `page_size` and `max_prefetch_pages` (default 0). prefetching complicates retries and memory; keep it off by default.

lisa: transport opt-in flag idea: `stream: "none" | "chunked" | "websocket"` — default `none` (plain page fetch). chunked behaves like HTTP streaming that yields the same `page` structure incrementally. websocket is entirely separate connection mode.

sdk-ci-bot: note: we have a failing test in `sdk-pager` job if we change default retry attempts — ensure test matrix includes python/ts/go with new defaults.

anya: action items:
- anya: draft RFC with: bookmark v1 semantics, retry defaults, transport modes, deprecation path for old cursor API.
- matt: write short migration notes for existing `cursor` users -> `bookmark`.
- juan: PR examples for py/ts/go iterator snippets to sync with docs.
- sophia: add explicit `retry: "none"` opt-out and docs for side-effect endpoints.
- lisa: run compatibility check with proxies/enterprise infra for chunked streaming.

matt: final comment — keep the surface intentionally small. no implicit magic resume across different clients (i.e., bookmarks are not interchangeable across API versions until server says so). thanks, will review RFC draft. :thumbsup:

anya: thanks all — i'll push the draft in ~24h and tag you. done for now.
